title: Letter 19 — How Great an Evil Is Sin
attribution_note: Letter 19 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: At your request I send you the composition in which is set forth how great an evil sin is — the same that you heard when you were with us in the monastery. Read it, and consider.

For a man there is nothing more profitable than to instruct himself how he may come to know and acknowledge his sin, and, for the sins already committed, having left them, to offer true sorrow unto God — the sacrifice of *“a broken spirit”* [Psalm 50:19] — and thenceforth to struggle against every sin, and by the power and help of God to overcome it, and to subject his own will to the will of God. For this above all does God require of us in His Word. Without this neither prayer, nor singing, nor offering can be acceptable unto God. For so long as a man abides in sins, he abides under the wrath of God; therefore all that he does is only *“an abomination before God,”* and so from his prayer, his singing and his offering God *“turneth away”* [Isaiah 1:13, 15; Micah 3:4].

A man must therefore leave his sins, and grieve that he has sinned, and thenceforth struggle against every sin, and not suffer sin to have dominion over him. Sin has dominion over a man when the man *“obeys it in the lusts thereof”* [Romans 6:12]. If, then, anyone commits fornication, or steals, or seizes what is another's by any means, or is malicious toward his neighbour and takes revenge upon him, or flatters, deceives, schemes, deals craftily, or curses, slanders, condemns his neighbour, or works any other unrighteousness — this is a sign that such a one is overcome by sin, and that sin has dominion over him. For he who hearkens to another and obeys him, by that other is possessed, as the apostle says: *“of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage”* [2 Peter 2:19]. So he who hearkens to sin and obeys it is possessed by it, and serves it, according to the word of the Lord: *“Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin”* [John 8:34].

sections.heading: How a man hearkens to sin

pairs.en: You will ask: how does a man hearken to sin and obey it?

Answer. *“Out of the heart proceed evil thoughts”* [Matthew 15:19], and they urge a man either to fornication, or to malice and revenge, or to plunder, and the rest; and when the man consents to this — he hearkens to sin and obeys it.
How then shall a man struggle against sin?

Answer. Not to consent to the evil thought; and as soon as it arises, to cut it short and put it to death. In this consists the whole Christian struggle. And since of ourselves we cannot do this — for we are very weak, and have a corrupt heart, and to struggle against sin and overcome it is nothing other than to overcome one's own heart, one's own nature, and oneself, which for every man is most difficult, as each may see — therefore the help of God is without fail needful in this. And that the help of God may come to us, and always help us and strengthen us in that struggle, frequent and humble prayer is needful, petition and sighing.

To sin and to please the flesh is as easy as to float with the current of a river; but to stand against sin, to put it to death and overcome it, is for us of ourselves as hard as to swim against the current without oarsmen or a sail with a favourable wind. He who would swim against the current of a river must without fail have either oarsmen, or a sail with a favourable wind; so he who would stand against sin, struggle and overcome it, and *“live godly in Christ Jesus”* [2 Timothy 3:12], needs the power of the Holy Spirit, helping, strengthening and urging him on. For by nature every man is drawn to the pleasing of the flesh, to the pleasing of his own will, to self-love and to every sin; and to resist this inclination and overcome it is for a man of himself impossible.

For this, as was said above, fervent prayer is needful, a turning of the heart away from the love of the world, a frequent remembrance of death and of eternity blessed and of eternity wretched, a meditation upon the attributes of God — His almighty power, goodness and majesty — together with the consideration of who sins, and against Whom: man, earth and dung, sins against the majesty of God and offends Him. Such consideration can strike a man with fear, and turn him from sin, and bring him to true contrition (of which in the following points a brief account is given and explained, that it may be better understood).
Also needful is the reading or hearing of Holy Scripture and of other books profitable to the Christian soul.
If a man sins of his free will, he sins heavily — which is known from the following points.
1) Who is man? Earth and dung.
Who is God? The Creator of all creation, of things visible and invisible.

How does he sin before God? He will not fulfil His will and commandment. God commands man: honour thy father and mother, and all authority; be not malicious and avenge not; kill not; commit not adultery; steal not; speak not evil; condemn not; slander not thy neighbour; desire not another's goods — but man hearkens not to this commandment of God, and stands stubbornly against God and his Creator, and the holy commandments which He *“hath commanded to keep diligently”* [Psalm 118:4] he breaks without fear and with boldness. And what is wonderful — or rather, what is worthy of pity — is this: the same sinner dares not transgress the commands of an earthly king or of his master, yet the commands of God, the King of kings and Lord of lords, he transgresses without fear!

Look and consider, O man, how heavily you sin: for what is a king or a high master before God? As nothing; for all men are *“earth and ashes”* [Ecclesiasticus 10:9]. God alone has dominion over all; for His sake one must obey the king, and the master, and every authority. It is praiseworthy that you hearken to your king and your master; but it is lawless and godless that you hearken not to God, before Whom the king, and the master, and every authority bend the knee. For what is this, if not to honour the creature more than the Creator, and man more than God?

2) Our God is in every place, as the omnipresent One who filleth all things, and all that is done is done before His holy eyes. So also His holy commandments are broken before His eyes. Who will dare to behave himself unseemly before an earthly king or before his master? Only a madman. But you, O man, dare to behave yourself unseemly before the majesty of God, destroying His holy law, and render not the honour due to His infinite holiness! You see how heavily you sin against the Lord your God.

O, if a man would consider what affront and offence he does thereby to the goodness of God, and what ruin he brings upon his own soul, he would turn from every sin with all diligence, and would tremble, and for past sins would weep and wail without comfort. But, blinded by the malice of the devil, he neither sees nor marks this.

Cease, then, O man, to destroy the law of God before God, lest you come to know upon yourself His righteous judgment, and taste the lawful curse which smites the sinner with temporal and eternal punishment. You are careful not to behave yourself unseemly before your master and your authority: how much more must you be careful, cautious, and fearful before the omnipresent majesty of God, and walk orderly.
O Lord! Open the eyes of our hearts, that we may see Thy fearful glory, and give glory to Thy fearful and holy name.

3) God holds heaven, and earth, and the whole world, and you, O man, in His almighty hand; to Him the Angels bow with fear and fulfil His will with all diligence; of Him the demons and all hell tremble, for *“the devils also believe, and tremble”* [James 2:19]; before Him *“the earth shook”* [Psalm 67:9], the sea flees and the rivers are turned back [see Psalm 113:3]; and every creature serves Him and fulfils His command. But you, O man, cease not to anger and provoke so fearful a God! Great is your fearlessness, boldness and frenzy — to provoke Him in whose hand is your life and your death, who is able to cast you down into hell in the very act of sin!
4) Man, when he sins, shows great ingratitude toward God.
From whom have you your being, O man? From God.
From whom are your body and your soul? From God.

From whom is all your frame? From God, as David sings unto God: *“My substance was not hid from Thee”* [Psalm 38:8]. God did not create you a beast, a wild animal, a bird, a fish, a tree, or any other senseless and speechless thing, but created you a man, and honoured you with a reasonable soul.
From whom do you receive food, drink, clothing, a house, and the other goods? From God.
Whose light, sun, moon and stars give you light? God's.
Whose water waters you and washes you? God's.
Whose fire warms you and cooks your food? God's.
Whose clouds sprinkle water upon you? God's.
Whose cattle, birds, fishes, trees and herbs serve your needs? All are God's.
Who commanded the earth to bring forth divers fruits, and for whose sake? God, for your sake.

To whom does all the rest of creation serve by the command of God? To you. For the creation of God serves not for its own sake, but for ours. Not for itself do the sun and the stars shine, but for us. Not for itself does the earth bring forth fruit, but for us; and so with the rest. Neither is it for God's sake, for God has no need of this service. Therefore all the creation of God serves us, that we may offer unto the Creator thanksgiving, praise, and a reasonable service, and serve Him by faith and love.

For whose sake was that great deed accomplished — that is, the incarnation of the Son of God? For whose sake did He come into the world, was born in the flesh, suffer and die? For you, and for me, and for every man. For God *“regardeth not persons”* [Deuteronomy 10:17; Luke 20:21], but for every man — for you and for me, and for all — He sent His Son into the world, that all by His grace might be saved.
For whose sake, then, was He born, did He suffer and die? For you and for me, O man.
To whom did He open heaven with all its treasure by His death? To me and to you, O man.

If, then, a man sins and works iniquity, he despises all these benefits of God, and shows himself most ungrateful toward God his Benefactor, and grievously offends, angers and provokes Him; and does as one who reviles and insults his benefactor — the man who feeds him, clothes him and preserves him.

Great is our folly and frenzy, that we provoke and grieve Him from whom we receive all things, and our very being. Many men, and even the beasts, are grateful to their benefactors: the dog honours his master and feeder; and this we read even of wild beasts in the histories. But the wretched sinner is so blinded that he honours not God, his Creator and highest Benefactor (for without love and fear it is impossible to honour God), but always provokes Him, and therefore becomes worse than the very cattle and the wild beast, though he is endowed with reason. Such ingratitude of his, and the benefit of God despised by him, will accuse him in the day of Judgment; and his own conscience will rise up against him, and will tear him, accuse him and torment him.

What if God should take away the light from us? Should we not wander as the blind? Or if He took away fire? Should we not all freeze? Or if He took away food, drink and air? Should we not all perish? Without air a man cannot live even a minute. So great a good is every creature, that without it we cannot live; and we know it then, when we are deprived of it. How great a good is bread, in the time of famine. How great a good is water, in the time of thirst. How great a good is fire, in the cold. How great a good is light, we know in darkness, and the rest. But the sinner, enjoying these and the other goods of God, honours not God his Benefactor, but ceases not to offend and provoke Him.
God does good to man, but man angers God his Benefactor. God ceases not from well-doing; man ceases not from malice and ingratitude. With such blindness is poor man smitten!

Wonderful is the goodness of God, which does good even to His enemies! Wonderful is the blindness and hardness of the sinner, who is softened neither by forgiveness nor by the well-doing of God! Therefore man himself is to blame when God takes His good from him. *“The Lord is upright, and there is no unrighteousness in Him”* [Psalm 91:15; Deuteronomy 32:4]. Whenever we suffer any evil or calamity, we ourselves are to blame that we are deprived of the goods of God; for we ourselves make ourselves unworthy — we to whom God always desires to do good, even though we are unworthy, and ceases not to do good.

5) God, as most good and a lover of mankind, greatly desires and longs to save man and make him eternally blessed, as is plain from all Holy Scripture — so much so that He spared not His only-begotten Son for our salvation, O people; but the devil, as the adversary of God and our enemy, desires to destroy man and to cast him again into that eternal ruin from which Christ by His Blood delivered him, and he catches man into that ruin through pleasure, luxury and sin, as with a hook. But man, blinded, leaving the saving will of God, follows the ruinous will of the devil, and snatches at sin as a fish at the hook, and stands fast in sin, and will not truly repent, and so chooses ruin for himself rather than salvation (for without true repentance it is impossible to be saved), and so grievously offends God, who loves our soul.
Look, O man, how an unrepentant life offends God!

6) The devil, making war upon our Creator and being able to do nothing against Him, turns upon man, and through him strives to blaspheme and dishonour the name of God; and for this he draws man to the transgression of the commandments of God, that so the Lawgiver may be despised. Man, not understanding this, hearkens to the enemy, destroys the commandments of God, and by the transgression of the commandments dishonours Him who gave them, as the apostle says: *“through breaking the law thou dishonourest God”* [Romans 2:23] — and so becomes an instrument of the devil, by which the name of God is dishonoured. So our first parents in paradise, hearkening to the devil and despising God who gave the commandment, dishonoured Him [see Genesis 3]. So also now the Christian, despising the commandments of God and hearkening to the devil, dishonours Him who commanded. For as by good works, done in honour of the name of God, the name of God is glorified, so by the evil works of Christians it is dishonoured.
O, how heavy and fearful is this!... Only *“them that honour Me I will honour, and they that despise Me shall be lightly esteemed,”* saith the Lord [1 Samuel 2:30].

Tell me, I pray you: would it not be a dishonour and a great affront to you, if a servant of yours, honoured by you, despising your order, should hearken to your enemy and adversary? What greater frenzy can there be? So does the sinner, who, despising the commandments of the Lord his God, hearkens to the adversary of God — the devil; for he is the first adversary and rebel against his Creator, and into that same God-hated work he craftily and cunningly drew man [see Genesis 3].

7) The devil deceives and leads a man to the destruction of the commandments of God; but for this he also *“accuseth”* the man *“before our God,”* wherefore he is called *“the accuser of our brethren”* [Revelation 12:10]. Great is this snare, craft and cunning of the subtle spirit! He entices to sin, and accuses for sin — seeking nothing other than the ruin of man. Our God, deliver us from this deceiver! Blind man, not considering this, snatches at sin as at something pleasant, and is thereby wounded and perishes, like little children who snatch without sense at burning coals, are burned, and afterwards suffer and weep.

8) As a visible enemy, having overcome his adversary and taken him captive, mocks and laughs at him, so our invisible enemy the devil, having taken the Christian captive by sin, holds him as a prisoner, laughs and makes sport of him, and often from sin to sin and from lust to lust, as wheat, sows him and tosses him — now to the love of money, now to the love of glory, now to the love of pleasure; and so, having entangled him in the lusts of the world, holds him as a fish in a net, and laughs at him, until he cast him into the uttermost ruin in which he himself abides.

9) When the sinner by the grace of God comes to himself and begins to repent and to seek mercy of God, then the enemy strives to bring him to despair, setting before him the justice of God, which renders to all according to their works. “Such and such an evil,” he says, “have you done: how then shall you be saved? God will not receive you, because you have destroyed His commandments. For this righteous Judge will render to all according to their works; He will render also to you according to your evil deeds. Why then should you hope, and look for mercy from Him?” — and the rest. So the subtle spirit, as before sins he sets the mercy of God before a man, that he may cast him into sins, so to the one who has sinned he sets the justice of God before him, that he may bring him to despair; and so by every means he strives to destroy us. Therefore the apostle exhorts us: *“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”* [1 Peter 5:8].

sections.heading: What Scripture says of the lawless

pairs.en: 10) Holy Scripture speaks fearfully of those who work iniquity. *“But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare My statutes, or that thou shouldest take My covenant in thy mouth?* *Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest My words behind thee”* [Psalm 49:16–17] — that is, My words, which you ought to have before you, to remember, love, honour as the words of My mouth, and by their rule to order and lead your life — these, O sinner, you have cast behind you, and look not upon them. Behold what the sinner does: he casts behind him the words of God, which he ought to have before him, and look upon them as in a mirror, and cleanse his faults!

Again it says: the lawless *“have not set God before them”* [Psalm 53:5; 85:14]. And yet more fearfully God speaks through the prophet: *“They have turned unto Me the back, and not the face”* [Jeremiah 32:33]. That is, they ought, as My creatures and My servants, turning unto Me, to honour Me as their Creator, God and Lord, to bow down, and to attend to what I say and command, and to fulfil it; but they, the lawless, have turned away from Me and turned to the creature, to the world, to sin and to the devil, and please him. For he who hearkens to another, pleases that other.

And further He calls those who work iniquity children of the devil. *“Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do”* [John 8:44; 1 John 3:7–10]. Look and consider, O man, whose you are, though you bear the name of Christ upon you. Without fail you are the son of him whose manners you portray, as the Lord says to the Jews: *“If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham”* [John 8:39]. And to whom you obey and whom you serve, of him are you the servant. Attend to this, and consider diligently, if you would not be condemned forever with the devil and suffer in hell!

11) The Christian man at Baptism renounced Satan and all his evil works, and promised to serve God *“in holiness and righteousness”* [Luke 1:75], and so, having left Satan, clave unto God. And God received him into His highest mercy, and washed him from the defilements of sins, sanctified and justified him, as it is written: *“ye are washed, ye are sanctified, ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God”* [1 Corinthians 6:11]. And the servant of God says to the baptized: “Thou art justified, thou art sanctified, thou art washed in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.” So washed, sanctified and justified, God received him for a son unto Himself, and made him heir of the heavenly kingdom, as His holy Word bears witness [see Romans 8:17; Galatians 4:7]. The Christian, when he turns again to sin and serves the lusts of the world, again falls away from God and cleaves to Satan and his evil works. For *“no man can serve two masters,”* saith the Lord [Matthew 6:24]. And then there is weeping among the Angels and all the saints, who before rejoiced at his salvation and blessedness.

O sinner! Wherein has the Lord your God not pleased you, that you have left Him? He created you and honoured you with a reasonable soul; He feeds you, clothes you and supplies you with the other goods; He sent His Son into the world for your sake and delivered Him up to death; He washed you, justified and sanctified you by the laver of regeneration, and made you heir of eternal blessedness; and He desires to dwell in you as in His house and temple, if only He see a place pleasing to Him in your soul. And wherein does the devil please you, who desires to bring you with himself into eternal ruin, that you fulfil his will? For this is his continual care, as our true enemy. Turn, then, to your Father from whom you have gone away, and cast yourself before His merciful eyes, and confess with the prodigal son: *“Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before Thee”!* He waits for you, and is ready to receive you, and to clothe you in the best robe, and there will be *“joy in the presence of the angels of God”* over you also *“that repenteth,”* according to the word of the Lord. The merciful Heavenly Father will say of you also: *“This my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found”* [Luke 15:7, 10–32]. Come, O sinners! *“O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.* *For He is our God”* [Psalm 94:6–7].

sections.heading: Why this evil still pleases you

pairs.en: 12) You see, O sinner, how heavy and ruinous an evil sin is. Why then does this evil please you? Why will you not turn from it, and break without fear the holy and eternal law of God, which was given us for this very end, that we should keep it whole? Do you say in your heart, *“There is no God”* [Psalm 13:1]? Or do you think that He sees not your sins and iniquities? Or do you think that He will not render according to their works to the righteous and the sinful? Or do you flatter yourself that God will bear with you in your sins? Or know you not, and have you not yet proved, what the fire of Gehenna is, and eternal torment? Or do you dream some other thing of the like kind? All this is a lawless thought.

How is there no God, of whom the whole world preaches [see Psalm 18:1–7; Acts 14:17; Romans 1:20]? How knows He not your sins, who gave you reason, eyes and ears? *“He that planted the ear, shall He not hear?* *He that formed the eye, shall He not see?* *He that chastiseth the heathen, shall not He correct”* [Psalm 93:9–10]? How shall He not render according to their works, who is eternal Righteousness?

Who drowned the lawless with the waters, and preserved the righteous man in the ark? Who burned Sodom and Gomorrah the lawless, and snatched righteous Lot from thence and preserved him? Who led Israel through the sea, and drowned Pharaoh with all his host? Who saved the godly youths in the Babylonian furnace, and burned the ungodly round about the furnace? Who saved the other godly, and punished the ungodly? God, God, who will render to all according to their works. He, as the Righteous One, will in the age to come also render to every man according to his works. Piety shall be rewarded, and ungodliness punished. To the righteous there shall be life, and to the sinful eternal torment.

If, because God still bears with you, as He has borne, you cease not to sin — what shall be, if this hope prove false, if He bear no longer, if in the very midst of that lawless dreaming He smite you righteously? It shall be with you as it has befallen others: as it befel in the time of the flood, or as with the men of Sodom, or with Pharaoh, or as with Dathan and Abiram, whom the earth swallowed up alive [Psalm 105:17; Numbers 16:31], or as with Ananias and Sapphira who lied, who fell down suddenly without breath [Acts 5:5, 10], or as still befalls those who work iniquity. But if God bear with you further — for not all the lawless are punished here, according to the unsearchable judgments of God — then you heap up for yourself more of the wrath of God and of eternal punishment.

O man! *“Or despisest thou the riches of His goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?* *But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; who will render to every man according to his deeds”* — so the apostle speaks to you [Romans 2:4–6]. Or would you prove what the wrath of God is, and eternal torment? You shall prove it, if you cease not to sin and repent not; you shall prove it, but then you shall not be able to free yourself from it, though you earnestly desire, but shall pay therein for all your committed sins without end. For then repentance shall cease and mercy shall be ended; then shall be heard the voice: *“Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”* [Luke 16:25].

Now men suffer either in sickness, or in prison, or in exile, or in captivity, or in some other thing; but from these calamities they are delivered either before death, or by death. But from that calamity, sickness, sighing, prison, captivity, torment and suffering they can never be delivered. Then they will desire death, but will not be able to die.

Behold whither fearlessness and an unrepentant life lead! Therefore now, while you have not yet proved this, know and acknowledge your sins, and leave them, and repent, that you may not prove and taste that bitterness, but may obtain mercy from God — which I desire from the heart both for myself and for every man.
You see how fierce and ruinous an evil sin is, though men love it. Guard yourself, then, beloved, against it, as against the poison of a serpent.
Save thyself.
